title: roost agent state (v1)
description: The single reconciled state of every agent, published retained to the state topic. Produced only by the roost daemon; every renderer is a subscriber and never aggregates.
comment-on-additional-properties: additionalProperties is deliberately true. Renderers MUST tolerate unknown fields so the daemon can add them without a coordinated release.

v.description: Schema version. Renderers should refuse to interpret a payload whose major version they do not know.

ts.description: Publication time, second resolution, UTC. ABSENT on the Last Will payload: the will is fixed at connect time, so any timestamp in it would be arbitrarily stale by the time the broker sent it. A payload with state 'offline' and no 'ts' means 'offline as of now'.

state.description: Displayed state. Aggregated by precedence: needs_attention > stalled > thinking > listening > idle. 'offline' is never produced by aggregation; only the broker publishes it, via Last Will.

count.description: Number of NON-IDLE agents. Not the total number of agents.

label.description: Short human-readable line, from the agent that determined the displayed state. Truncated to 64 characters IN THE DAEMON, at this schema boundary; a truncated value ends with U+2026. A renderer may ellipsize further to fit its glass but must never receive a longer string. The cap is a feature, not a budget: a label that had to be truncated, or that is missing entirely, forces any accompanying prompt to kind 'handoff', because approving a question you could not read in full is the failure the cap exists to prevent.

urgency.description: Maximum urgency across all NON-IDLE agents. Computed independently of which agent won the state race, so a quietly-thinking agent that is blocking still raises this.

primary_run_id.description: Run id of the agent that determined the displayed state. Renamed from 'run_id' before v1 shipped: the old name implied a single run in a payload that aggregates many.

since.description: When the winning agent entered its current state. Additive to v1. Elapsed time is derived from this, NOT from 'ts', which is publication time and would reset on every heartbeat. Null when nothing is running. Renderers predating this field ignore it and fall back to their own first-seen time.

prompt.description: An open question from the agent named by 'primary_run_id', answerable from a surface that supports it. Additive to v1. NULL means the daemon supports prompts and there is none; ABSENT means the daemon predates the field. A renderer that does not understand this field shows 'needs_attention' with no buttons, which is the correct fallback: it says something needs you and sends you to a laptop.

id.description: Identifies the QUESTION, not the run. Distinct from 'primary_run_id' because one run can ask several questions in sequence, so answering has to name the question. An answer for an id the daemon has already resolved must be rejected by the daemon, never by the browser.

kind.description: What controls to draw. 'approve_reject' draws two buttons. 'handoff' draws NONE: the question exists but cannot be answered here, so the surface says a decision is waiting and sends you to read it properly elsewhere. That is designed behaviour, not a failure state. A renderer MUST treat an unknown kind as no prompt rather than guessing at controls, which is what makes adding a kind safe: a renderer that does not know 'handoff' shows needs_attention with no buttons, which is already almost the right rendering.

reversible.description: Whether one tap is enough. False requires a deliberate second confirm. ASSERTED BY THE DAEMON: a renderer must never infer this from the label text, because a renderer that infers it will eventually infer it wrong and silently one-tap something destructive.

expires_at.description: When this question dies on its own. The independent backstop for a panel that stops hearing from the daemon: past this the panel dims the buttons with no new message required. The daemon also drops an expired prompt at aggregation, so the two mechanisms cover different failures. Null means no expiry was supplied.
